name: Mesh Topology and Robust Digitization
text:
# Mesh Topology and Robust Digitization
## Overview
This family of methods converts polygon meshes into discrete volumetric representations (voxel grids) while prioritizing topological validity and robustness against geometric defects [G]. Unlike standard [rasterization](#15310-rasterization.md) which may produce gaps or artifacts on non-watertight or low-quality meshes, these techniques enforce structural integrity, ensuring the resulting volume accurately reflects the mesh's interior or surface connectivity [G]. They differ from primitive-based union methods by treating the mesh as a unified solid object rather than a collection of independent bounding volumes [G].
## Shared principles

## Subtopics

### [Relaxed Connectivity Voxelization](2481-relaxed-connectivity-voxelization.md)
Produces a binary `UniformGrid` from effectively 1D primitives (curves, surfaces) where occupied voxels form a 26-connected path [G]. It distinguishes itself by using a target of three bisecting quadrilaterals per voxel to guarantee connectivity without gaps, unlike standard methods that may break thin structures [G]. Choose this for flow simulation or fill operations on thin structures where topological continuity is critical [G].

### [Polygon Mesh Voxelization via Union of Sets](4605-polygon-mesh-voxelization-via-union-of-sets.md)
Transforms a polygon mesh into a `UniformGrid` using high-level library abstractions (e.g., PyVista) [G]. It enforces topological validity through built-in watertightness checks [G]. Distinguished from explicit geometric [decomposition](#7254-decomposition.md) methods, it relies on library functions like `pyvista.voxelize` [G]. Choose this for rapid [voxelization](#12-voxelization.md) of valid, watertight meshes where ease of implementation is preferred over low-level control [G].

### [Labeled Volume Creation via MultiBlock Iteration](7389-labeled-volume-creation-via-multiblock-iteration.md)
Produces a single `RectilinearGrid` from a `MultiBlock` mesh input, labeling each voxel with the integer ID of the specific sub-mesh block it intersects [G]. It differs from [binary voxelization](#2402-sdf-based-binary-voxelization.md) by preserving the topological identity of each mesh component through iterative enclosed-point testing or data sampling [G]. Choose this when distinguishing between multiple overlapping or adjacent mesh components in a single volume is required [G].

### [Improved Tetrahedral Mesh Generation for Voxelization](7476-improved-tetrahedral-mesh-generation-for-voxelization.md)
A robust framework that generates a high-quality tetrahedral mesh within a user-defined error bound to produce solid binary voxel data [G]. It specifically addresses the failure of existing methods on low-quality, non-watertight, or topologically open meshes [G]. Unlike centroid-connection methods, it combines background grid insertion with mesh improvement to maintain quality and speed, achieving near 100% success rates on difficult datasets [G]. Choose this for robust voxelization of internet-sourced 3D models that are often non-watertight or low-quality [G].

### Displacement Voxelization
**Definition**: An extension to the base framework that uses PN-triangles and displacement mapping to voxelize low-resolution meshes with rugged surfaces at high resolution, achieving visual quality comparable to conventional voxelization of high-resolution meshes [S1, unofficial].
**Steps**: Perform triangle subdivision using the hardware tessellator as in the base method [S1, unofficial]. Use PN-triangles to reconstruct mesh details [S1, unofficial]. Utilize the positions and normals of the PN-triangles to apply displacement mapping during the voxelization process [S1, unofficial].

## Background
The need for robust [mesh voxelization](#6514-mesh-voxelization.md) arises from the prevalence of low-quality, non-watertight, or topologically open meshes in internet 3D models, which cause standard voxelization methods to fail [G]. Displacement voxelization was developed to maintain visual quality while achieving higher performance by voxelizing low-resolution versions of triangle meshes [S1, unofficial]. It compares efficiency with pipeline-based and CUDA-based methods [S1, unofficial].
